newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Key Nigeria refinery at risk over maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Key Nigeria refinery at risk over maintenance.

text.p: Nigeria's newer Port Harcourt refinery, the country's most modern stands the risk of developing technical problems because of the inability of the authorities to carry out its turn around maintenance, the state news agency NAN reported on Tuesday.
It said the 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) plant last underwent the comprehensive maintenance in 1994 and should normally have one every two years to save it from damage.

NAN said its investigations had shown it would require $27 million to carry out the maintenance for the refinery while $12 million was needed to service an older refinery located in the same city in the oil-producing southeast.
Nigeria's four refineries already operate at a fraction of their installed capacity because of breakdowns and lack of funds to repair them.
The result has been incessant fuel shortage in Africa's leading oil-producing nation.

NAN said engineering experts had called on the federal government to carry out the turn-around maintenance of the Port Harcourt refinery early next year at the latest because it was the only one sustaining the nation's fuel supplies.
